charter.title: CHARTER — what the Confluence atlas already does, and what the operative-content graph must do instead
charter.oneParagraph: The Great Confluence (assets/js/core/data/confluence.js) is a TRANSMISSION map: 190 entries across nine fixed lanes and 155 typed, epistemically-labelled edges whose whole claim is that one thing was demonstrably read, rendered, answered or absorbed by another — 'the atlas plots INFLUENCE, never validity', edge kinds translation | influence | commentary | synthesis | refutation | adaptation, each edge carrying label (documented 145 / disputed 9 / debunked 1), bestCitation and a note grading the transmission claim itself, with the debunked edge drawn faint-and-struck rather than hidden. Its 91 `technique` fields are a single free-text prose sentence per entry — untyped, ungraded, unsegmented, and attached indiscriminately to text, person, event, institution and translation nodes; they answer 'what did this tradition do?' and nothing else. The operative-content graph answers a different question and must not restate the first: it types WHICH PROCEDURE-KINDS a work contains (controlled vocabulary), HOW COMPLETE the text's own account is (complete | partial | referenced | fragmentary, each with named missing elements and the evidence for the grade), and HOW A PROCEDURE — not a book — propagates, which is a strictly stronger claim than an influence edge and requires its own citation (the repo contains exactly one such claim already: Mallinson's derivation of the mahāmudrā/mahābandha/mahāvedha trio from the Amṛtasiddhi into the Dattātreyayogaśāstra). THE JOIN KEY IS THE CONFLUENCE `slug`: every work in the new graph that exists in the atlas must carry the atlas slug verbatim (103 of the 127 procedure-bearing works inventoried here do; the other 24 — the whole abhicāra corpus bar the Atharvaveda, three rasa texts, every greatworks-only work, and the three computed divination engines — do NOT, and must either mint a namespaced id or trigger an atlas entry), so the two graphs cross-link on slug and neither owns the other — the atlas answers 'who read whom', the operative graph answers 'what does this text tell an operator to do, how fully, and where did that sequence come from'.

joinKey.rule: Reuse verbatim where an atlas entry exists. Where none exists, mint an id in a declared namespace (this file uses abh:, rasa:, gw:, gwe:, div:) and record joinKeyStatus so the synthesizer can see at a glance which works need an atlas entry.

structuralGaps: No completeness dimension exists anywhere in shipped data. Not one record in the repo says whether a text gives a full sequence, a partial one, a mere reference, or a fragment. This is the new graph's entire reason to exist and it has NO prior art to inherit — grades must be evidenced from scratch.

The atlas `technique` field is attached to 91 entries of which many are person / event / institution / translation nodes, not works (e.g. person-abulafia, quanzhen, naqshbandi-order, event-shangqing-revelations, event-mbsr-1979, event-golden-flower-1929). The new graph must decide whether procedures may hang off non-work nodes, and must resolve at least two mis-attributions the atlas already contains: the Mevlevi samāʿ is attached to the Masnavī though the atlas's own body says it was codified after Rumi's death; and event-golden-flower-1929 (a translation node) restates the source text's technique verbatim.

Only ONE edge anywhere in the repo is a genuine procedure-propagation claim (amrtasiddhi→dattatreyayogasastra, Mallinson 2020, naming the three practices). The other 44 both-endpoints-procedure-bearing atlas edges are work-level influence claims that MUST NOT be silently upgraded.

There is no cross-module identity layer at all — mudras.js `source:"gheranda"|"hyp"` likewise resolves to atlas slugs only by human inference.

Harm notes exist at page level (abhichara FRAMING/care, RASA_TOXICITY, Picatrix BOOK_IV flags, MAGIC_DISCLAIMER, REMEDIES_FRAMING) and at record level for 6 of 35 mudrās, but nothing types the hazard kind (toxic substance / hypoxia / self-injury / coercion / sleep-deprivation / sexual content / living-tradition sensitivity).

works.title: Cantong qi (Seal of the Unity of the Three)
works.author: Wei Boyang (attributed)
works.dateText: trad. c. 142 CE; received text formed by c. 450 CE (contested)
works.atlasTechnique: The text encodes elixir work in Yijing emblems: the trigrams Kan and Li stand for the ingredients ('true lead' and 'true mercury'), and lunar-cycle hexagram sequences set the timing of the 'fire phases.' Read as waidan it governs compounding actual mercury and lead — both documented severe poisons, described here for study only; read as neidan the same emblems map onto breath and inner essences.

works.atlasTechnique: The Shangqing scriptures instruct their adept to visualize gods residing in the body, to absorb the effulgences of sun, moon, and stars, and to undertake ecstatic spirit-journeys through the heavens — interior, imaginal disciplines replacing both congregational ritual and mineral elixirs.

works.title: Wuzhen pian (Awakening to Reality)
works.author: Zhang Boduan
works.atlasTechnique: The poems describe inner alchemy in symbolic terms: gathering 'true lead' and 'true mercury' — emblems for complementary aspects of the person, not the toxic metals — joining them in the 'tripod' of the body, and refining essence (jing) into breath (qi) and spirit (shen) through timed 'fire phases.' The physiology is symbolic; no physical elixir is compounded, and the text itself warns against ingesting minerals.

procedures.evidence: Atlas technique: neidan in symbolic terms — gathering "true lead"/"true mercury" as emblems for complementary principles. Repo explicitly frames the language as emblematic.

works.title: The Secret of the Golden Flower (Taiyi jinhua zongzhi)

procedures.evidence: Atlas technique: "turning the light around" (huiguang) — reversing attention back upon the source of awareness in seated stillness. Repo records the named method, not a staged sequence.

works.title: The Quanzhen (Complete Perfection) Order

procedures.evidence: Atlas technique: severe asceticism — sleep deprivation, begging — documented by Eskildsen and Komjathy.
procedures.harmNote: Sleep deprivation and fasting regimens: the atlas records them as documented historical asceticism; a harm note is REQUIRED on any expansion.
